historical_references.reference:
Jabed Khan was the last Nawab of Bengal in British Indian administration, ruling between 1760 and 1764 CE.
Context: Jabed Khan succeeded his father Alivardi Khan as the Nawab of Bengal. During his rule, the Marathas launched an invasion of Bengal, which led to significant losses for the Nawab. Jabed Khan was eventually forced to sign the Treaty of Allahabad in 1765, which recognized British supremacy in Bengal.

Jabed Shah, also known as Jabir bin Muhammad, was the founder of the Shia Jabari dynasty in Yemen in the mid-13th century CE.
Context: Jabed Shah was a Shia Muslim leader who established the Jabari dynasty in Yemen. He was a descendant of the Prophet Muhammad and claimed the title of Imam. The Jabari dynasty ruled Yemen until the mid-16th century CE.
